fields.v: Highest FPC rate 70.0% (Claude Code); mini-SWE-agent configurations pass checks on only 4.8-11.5% of valid outputs. All configurations below the Human Reference on Logic Patterns (0.0-1.3 vs 1.5); several exceed it on Documentation (Aider + GPT-4.1 8.1 vs 8.0), Error Handling, Library Constraints or Coding Style. Multi-file tasks reduce Coding Style (up to 1.4 pp), Error Handling (up to 1.7 pp) and Logic Patterns (up to 1.1 pp) improvements (all Table 4 S-M values positive for these three aspects), while Documentation sometimes increases (e.g. Claude Code 6.9 -> 9.3); two mini-SWE configurations have no eligible multi-file outputs. Aggregate NFI stable across runs (sd 0.1-0.4 for Codex, Claude Code, Aider). Claude Code uses ~100x the tokens of Codex for +5.2 pp FPC; cost per successful task 120.02 s / 424,970 tokens vs Codex 21.08 s / 4,339. Differences are descriptive (no significance testing)
fields.quote: While documentation occasionally benefits from additional cross-file context, multi-file tasks consistently reduce improvements in coding style (up to 1.4), error handling (up to 1.7), and logic patterns (up to 1.1).
fields.why: The RQ2 result omits the Coding Style reduction in multi-file tasks (up to 1.4), which the authors state in the RQ2 summary and Table 4 supports (all CS S-M values positive), and the Documentation increase.
fields.doubt: O resumo da RQ2 (pág. 8) diz que as tarefas multi-ficheiro reduzem também o Coding Style (até 1,4), e a Tabela 4 confirma (todas as diferenças S-M de CS são positivas). O teu resultado só refere EH e LP. Vê a Tabela 4 e decide se acrescentas CS (e o aumento em Documentation).
